title: A PreToolUse hook that means to block must actually block
origin: Both PreToolUse guards in .claude/settings.local.json read $CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT (never set — the payload is JSON on stdin) and exited 1 (non-blocking). They printed BLOCKED and let the command run, for as long as they existed.
prompt: Write a Claude Code PreToolUse hook that stops the agent editing any .env file. Give me the script and the settings.json entry.

checks.why: Only a permissionDecision of deny, or exit 2, blocks a tool call.
The payload arrives as JSON on stdin. A hook that does not read stdin cannot see what it is judging.
These environment variables are not set by Claude Code. A hook reading them sees an empty string and allows everything.
exit 1 is a non-blocking hook error. Printing BLOCKED and exiting 1 announces a block it is not performing.
